name: Penetration Slant Loop
formation: 11P Gun Spread 2x2 vs Even Speed Front
coverage: Cover 3 Buzz behind the slant-loop game

summary.motive: Win with pure penetration and staggered timing: tackles slant to occupy blockers while a delayed end loops through the gap their charge creates.
summary.keyDefender: The weak end executing the delayed loop
summary.whyItWorks: Slide protection must commit to the first visible threats, so the half-beat stagger guarantees one rusher arrives unblocked exactly where the protection has already left.
summary.failureMode: The running back keeps eyes inside and picks up the looper, leaving the quarterback a clean three-step throw to the flat valve.

beats.title: 1. The First Wave Slants
beats.text: Both defensive tackles fire instantly into the strong A and B gaps with a deliberate half-beat stagger, gluing the sliding offensive line to blocks it was already preparing to make.

beats.title: 2. The Delayed Loop Begins
beats.text: The weak end sells two steps of edge rush to pin the tackle and back, then pulls off the arc and starts his loop — Jimmy Johnson’s signature stagger that separates this stunt from every standard slant.

beats.title: 3. Protection Arithmetic Fails
beats.text: The slide protection accounts for the two visible slants and the containment rusher; the delayed looper is the sixth man in a five-man math problem, arriving through the vacated weak A-gap.

beats.title: 4. Loop Convergence Sack
beats.text: The stepping-up quarterback walks directly into the looping end while the B-gap tackle pushes the guard backward, finishing the penetration-first philosophy in a single picture.

relations.tell: The looping end takes two visible upfield steps and visibly gathers himself before redirecting inside — pure slant teams never pull off the arc.
